items.text: Raiders!
Update 2.3 is rolling out right now with the Noxious Set, a number of fixes and a new player project! Please restart the game to download.

Since Frozen Trail has released, we have been including fixes in our weekly updates. After today we will go back to the regular schedule of fixes every three weeks and store updates on a weekly basis.

While the four contradas of Toledo can’t agree on much, one thing they all have in common are the losses they’ve suffered topside. As brutal stories from Pendola Pass trickle into the cantinas, Celeste is encouraging members of Speranza to pause and honor the fallen. Remember each fallen Raider for who they were, and the dents they were able to make in ARC’s onslaught. Each offering is unique, but all who pause in reverence share in their Soul’s Offering.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41624047/8f89d162e867fd5eb9998fba36a88661bddcea67.jpg"]
Adjusted loot distribution in the Emperor. Containers near the entrance now yield lower-tier rewards, with higher-tier loot placed deeper inside.
Fixed a case where rolling enemies would continue to lay tracks after they died.
Improved the way ARC move when they are close to the borders of the map.
Fixed an issue where players could stand on the Skulker indefinitely.
Adjusted Vaporizer debris so they no longer fly away or jitter; responses now better match their weight and size.
Added new visual hatches to make it easier to see how far the Frigate puzzle has progressed.
Fixed missing collision on the Frigate that allowed players to enter or hide inside geometry, and prevented players getting stuck on the wings.
Minor animation adjustment to the Bull Rush skill’s camera animation on hit.
Fixed an issue where magazines did not eject during reloads on Bettina, Bobcat, and Kettle.
Added clearer audio cues on the Frigate’s power core vents and hatches to better signal progression, completion, and destruction states.
Added sound effects when picking up and placing furniture in the Outpost, including when returning furniture to its original slot.
Refined audio for Outpost crafting, placement, progress, and removal.
Fixed an issue where cloth would not simulate correctly.
General
Fixed an issue where downed Raiders continued to lose health after entering the Ballistic Gondola.
Increased Heavy Shield base charge value from 80 to 90.

Dev Note: We experimented with some small buffs to the Heavy Shield in the 2.0 update, and the data is showing us that the durability drain rate in particular showed marked changes. The usage rates for this shield are still relatively low, so we’re giving it another little bump, this time in the base charge value. This will slightly increase survivability against most weapons, without creating too large a margin between the Heavy and Medium Shields. We will continue to monitor the use of our various low-use equipment to try and find a balance that works for both usability and the overall game health, and will be monitoring this change closely for any unintended changes to overall combat balance.
When on or near the Frigate, pings now mark the exact location instead of labeling the Frigate.
Expanded on the exploit prevention feature used in locked rooms to provide a more fair experience inside the Emperor.
Blocked placing barricade kits where they intersect with solid walls or in spaces that are too tight.
Tweaked killboxes at the top of the compactor inside the Emperor in Pendola Pass to eliminate some scenarios where players would be unfairly killed.

Fixed an issue where heavy landings weren’t being triggered correctly when dodgerolling or when already in a heavy landing.and where retriggering a heavy landing during a Dodge Roll could negate fall damage; heavy landings now trigger correctly while rolling.
Fixed an issue where Scrappy would rotate in the Outpost outside of customization.
Fixed an issue where Scrappy would not appear in the Outpost until entering the Workshop or customization.
Frigate
You can now ping the Frigate from long range while it is entering the area.
Adjusted loot distribution so areas further in have a higher chance of higher-tier rewards;
Updated the cargo gate to a newer version.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41624047/d631384e275dc5f5da1f4be2758370f344cc9fe1.jpg"]
Fixed an issue where mines could be placed on dismantling barricades, causing them to float in midair.
Fixed an issue where fire from Flame Spray could pass through a wall.
Increased Flame Spray damage to 13/s (from 10/s) and reduced durability drain by 50%.
The Firefly Burner now activates on impact when thrown, traveling while leaving a trail of fire before exploding after about 3 seconds. Previously, it had to be shot to vent fire.
You can now use Adrenaline Shot even at max stamina. Its effect no longer stacks; using another Adrenaline Shot refreshes the duration.
Fixed inverted drop rates for furniture Designs; rarer items now drop less frequently.
Dolabra, Bobcat, Equalizer, Jupiter, Tempest, and Vulcano blueprints can now drop in any major map condition. Slightly lowered the drop chance of that pool to account for the increased value.
Reduced the drop chance of the Emperor Key blueprint from Redirection pods, and added a small chance to find ARC parts and high-tier ARC loot to compensate.
Grappling Hook
Fixed an issue where the Grappling Hook could not be used inside the Matriarch’s shield while it was active.
Tether items now affect players swinging from the grappling hook.
Fixed an issue where the Grappling Hook could launch players at extreme speeds or into the air when the line snagged on geometry, reducing unintended launches and falls.
Grappling hook now reattaches to debris when its target breaks apart, improving reliability when grappling destroyed ARC parts.

Fixed an issue where reeling an ARC with the Grappling Hook while the rope was wrapped around an obstacle pulled it toward the player instead of the wrap point; targets now reel toward the rope as intended, preventing unintended high‑speed launches.
Fixed an issue that allowed reeling in the Grappling Hook while firing was blocked, which could also corrupt the animation during a Dodge Roll.
Fixed a bug where the hand animation could get stuck after swapping from a thrown Grappling Hook to another item.
Camera
Added Color Push and Black & White filters to the advanced Camera.
Refined the film grain texture on the Classic Film filter.
Reduced depth-of-field blur on the Basic Camera to make selfies clearer.
Zipline
Fixed an issue where entering a zipline from the ground would not move the character upward, making attachments behave oddly. Characters now move upward correctly on entry.
Fixed an issue where the Zipline preview cable could disappear when aiming at very long distances.
Pendola Pass
Fixed multiple collision issues around the fallen Emperor in Pendola Pass to reduce getting stuck, missing collisions, and unintended out-of-bounds access.
Fixed an issue where players could sometimes clip through the gondola extraction on Pendola Pass.
Fixed missing ceiling collision in the Fallen Emperor on Pendola Pass that allowed players to leave the playable space.
Removed chairs in a shelter that could block looting due to collision issues.
Improved the placement of some containers inside the Storm Huts of Pendola Pass, which also fixes an issue with one of them where a Medical Bag could be interacted with through a wall.
Fixed an issue with an ammo box in Pendola Pass not being interactable.
Spaceport
Fixed an issue on Spaceport where players could get stuck when trying to pass through a small fence gap.
Stella Montis
Fixed various locations on Stella Montis where players could get stuck.
Updated FidelityFX Super Resolution (FSR) plugin to version 4.1.1.
Fixed an issue where Daily Quests did not refresh in the menus after they expired.
Reduced audio memory usage on Xbox Series S to improve stability and mitigate out-of-memory crashes, particularly when navigating around the Frigate.
Fixed an issue that could cause players to get stuck in the tunnel sequence after finishing a round; a failsafe now returns you to the front end if the end-of-round survey screen fails to load.
Added a workaround that mitigates a ray tracing related GPU crash on AMD RX 7000 series GPUs.
Reduced memory usage for the Frigate to address rare crashes when exploring its cargo hold with larger groups.
Improved stability when exploring the Frigate, reducing the chance of crashes.
Fixed a rare crash that could occur while using voice chat, improving overall voice chat stability.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41624047/93fa17e2d6115a4776ab48c816c412e79763912d.jpg"]
General
We will be disabling the Expedition Vault and you will receive Bronze Statuettes as compensation for the purchased slots. Everything you had in the Vault will be moved to your stash.
Fixed an issue where the HUD did not show the correct controller input hint for the Raider Tool and melee; it now displays the appropriate icon and Hold indicator based on your binding.
Camera HUD now extends to the edges of widescreen displays for a cleaner full-screen view.
The End of Round screen now correctly shows attached Weapon Mods and applied Stencils; tooltips correctly display applied Stencil info.

Fixed an issue where the mouse cursor could become confined to a small area after using the radial wheel with a controller, causing restricted cursor movement in inventory and looting interfaces when switching between mouse and controller.
Added animated transitions and a subtle glint effect to collection items in menus to improve visual feedback.
Unified On/Off toggle order in outfit customization: ON now appears first and OFF last across all items.
Added a camera bob option in Gameplay settings.
Fixed an issue where the health bar could display a healing preview while downed.
Codex
Fixed an issue where the selected Codex entry could be cut off in the sidebar; the selected entry now remains visible when scrolling.
Added a “Times Revived By A Stranger” stat to the Codex player stats page.
Fixed an issue where the Codex entry for “Bilguun’s Hideout” did not unlock after visiting it on Spaceport.
Updated the Basic and Advanced Camera tooltips to clarify where saved photos can be viewed in the Codex.
Outpost
Improved framing of Outpost furniture icons for clearer previews.
When placing furniture in the Outpost, camera cycling now skips views that don’t show a compatible slot for the selected item.
Fixed a camera issue at the Workshop Bench slot near the Outpost door that caused the view to clip through the wall.
Reward Pass
Improved the Reward Pass upgrade screen: standardized panel heights, adjusted padding, and capitalized "Includes:"; list items are larger to better support longer translations.
Updated the Reward Pass screen: improved the Feats panel layout, renamed Daily Feats to Feats and Weekly Bonus to Milestones, and refined timers for better readability.
Weapon Amplification
In the Amplification tree, branch points now list the specific amplifications they would block in the tooltip, replacing the generic exclusivity message.
The Amplify button in the Weapon Bench upgrade tab now shows its keybind when using keyboard and mouse.
Project
Resolved cases where the yellow dot on the Projects tab persisted after checking or starting projects.
Workshop
Reordered the Workshop subnavigation to match the tile order, placing Basic Workbench immediately after Scrappy.
Improved volumetric smoke visuals by reducing jitter and ensuring effects align more accurately with smoke density, resulting in more stable and coherent VFX
Improvements to skin shading.
Improved one of our ambient occlusion techniques that should significantly reduce ghosting and flickering of ambient occlusion in some areas
Added missing downwash visual effects when the Ballistic Gondola takes off.
Improved lighting on Frigates by preserving global illumination to prevent overly dark interiors.
The Raider Tool has the default skin even when other skins are equipped.
Extracting with partial progress of ‘To The Skies’ quest may result in an inability to complete it.
‘When Everything Falls’ - some quest objectives, such as “Photograph Port A” may not complete for some players.
In some instances, if players lose or sell quest items, such as the Equatorial Sundial needed for ‘Clean Hands’, the quest cannot be completed.
Some XBOX players may experience instability or crashes.
ARC Reclaimers can occasionally fail to dock on the appropriate spot on the Frigate.
When vaulting on an ARC Reclaimer, the player can be mistakenly pushed off.
Occasionally, some weapon models may increase in size dramatically during a raid.
Falling while using the Grappling Hook can cause the player to “bounce” high into the air.
There is a spot around the Railroad on Pendola Pass where players can get stuck.
See you Topside,
The ARC Raiders Team
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41624047/89205c54992a798d824e8033b257dfef0e514eed.jpg"]
Raiders!
Update 2.2 is rolling out right now with the Wreck Set and a number of fixes. Make sure to restart your game to download.
The PvE Beta test has wrapped up, and we hope you got the chance to jump in and try it out!

Now we’d love to hear what you thought. How did PvE compare to your usual experience? What could we improve? And how did the typical PvPvE experience change during the test? Share your thoughts in the dedicated PvE feedback channel on Discord.
We’ll also be sending a survey to a representative sample of ARC Raiders players starting October 22nd, so keep an eye on your inbox.
Read more here: PVE Test Thanks for Playing
General
Fixed an issue where the wind animations would not play on the Frigate.
Fixed an issue where the Vault Spring jump animation sometimes failed to play.
Fixed an issue where Selfie Emotes could appear distorted while moving.
Grappling Hook
Fixed an issue where swapping to a weapon immediately after throwing the Grappling Hook could cause weapon animations to break.
Polished climbing rope swing animations for smoother transitions when climbing up and jumping off.
The Grappling Hook throw animations now follow your up/down aim correctly, and the dodge roll animation while attached has been smoothed to prevent visual popping.
General
Fixed audio when opening and searching loot containers on the Frigate and inside the Emperor.
Tuned distance and air absorption for Frigate engine and Frigate Cannon audio to improve balance over range.
Adjusted blunt damage and debris impact sounds to be louder and scale properly.
Fixed missing looting sounds on Transmitter Debris objects.
Adjusted Bombardier mortar firing audio to reduce overly loud, close-sounding effects at long distances.
Polished Cassio’s and Celeste’s voice lines for improved clarity and consistency.
Added voice responses for the Cowboy emote.
Ballistic Gondola
Fixed an issue where Ballistic Gondola engine audio could drop out during takeoff, ensuring continuous rocket sound.
Extended the Ballistic Gondola takeoff preparation sound to prevent it from cutting off when multiple players board in sequence.
Added distant variations of Ballistic Gondola boarding and takeoff alarms to improve audio positioning and distance cues.
Polished Ballistic Gondola door interaction sounds and fixed an issue where the door open sound could play twice when entering and exiting.
Fixed an issue where certain ARC could be more accurate than intended against sliding players; their aim now correctly accounts for sliding targets.

Fixed an issue where the Hydra's weapons wouldn't spread to different targets as often as intended. We've increased the base damage to compensate for this corrected targeting behavior, ensuring its overall threat level remains competitive. We've also addressed an issue where it struggled to hit close-range targets.
ARC will now react to Gondola Transceivers being interacted with.
Frigate
Fixed an issue where players could be ejected from the cargo while it was falling from the Frigate.
Fixed an issue where you could be instantly knocked out when riding on the side of a Frigate cargo drop. Being crushed now only applies at the landing point, and riders inside.
Fixed an issue where Raiders riding on a Frigate cargo drop could be burned during descent; thruster heat now only affects areas near landing.
Emperor
Fixed an issue where moving platforms inside the Emperor could become out of sync, improving reliability when riding or crossing them.
General
Fixed an issue where Tether Launchers could not be repaired in-round.
Fixed an issue where the Geometric Fabric Chair Design blueprint was not granted after consuming it.
Grappling Hook
Improved the experience of rappeling to the ground with the Grappling Hook.
Improved auto-vaulting from Grappling Hook, made the wall detection more reliable and work more consistent on steep slopes.

notes.title: Improved swing and rope-climb entry near the ground

items.text: Climbing continues briefly when starting a climb from the ground.
Velocity toward the rope is preserved, so jumping from the ground carries into a climb.
Attaching to a rope on a steep slope now enters the wall-climb state.
Fixed unintended landing when climbing beneath an overhead rope.
General

Increased the spawn consistency of ARC Turbines in Buried City, Riven Tides, Blue Gate and Spaceport; in sessions where they previously only had a chance of spawning, they should now instead spawn in an overwhelming majority of, if not all, sessions.
Fixed visual culling on Frigate lighting scenarios in Buried City, Spaceport, Blue Gate, and Adjusted map boundaries near the Emperor to prevent players from clipping out of bounds.
Fixed some issues with the coverage of the compaction killboxes inside the Emperor.
Pendola Pass
Fixed a collision issue that could cause players to get stuck inside the Fallen Emperor.
Increased the enemy presence slightly.
Improved lighting and reflections to enhance visual clarity across multiple weather scenarios.
Fixed an issue with a Ballistic Gondola navigating through the Secure Communications Mast.
Fixed floating objects, vegetation and snow clipping through walls.
Fixed multiple locations where players could get stuck or fall through the terrain.
Dam Battlegrounds
Removed ARC Turbine spawns from standard sessions and most minor map conditions. In the remaining conditions, they should now spawn in an overwhelming majority of, if not all, sessions.
Stella Montis
Improved lighting and reflections to enhance visual clarity and consistency across time-of-day scenarios.
Jumping off the wall during a Wall Run now requires holding backward to activate to help avoid triggering it accidentally.
Enabled interactions from wall climbing to allow transitioning into ladders and ziplines.
Reduced memory usage from loot spawning systems to improve overall stability during rounds.
Optimized the Frigate entry sequence.
“To the Skies” can be completed on any map no matter where progress has been made, players only need to complete the installation in one location to complete the quest.
“Belly of the Beast” optional objective now requires the correct item as described in the objective text.
Reduced memory usage in Frigate interiors to address rare crashes when exploring the cargo hold.
Improved stability in the Frigate by fixing a memory issue that could lead to crashes when moving through its interior.
General
Polished Main Menu lighting and reflections for improved visuals.
Removed the Expedition Vault tab and related offer.
Quest
Fixed an issue where focus could be lost when navigating the quest tracker with a gamepad.
Reward Pass
Fixed an old Cred icon showing up in character customization for Reward Pass rewards.
Feats rebalance: We’ve added new Feats, removed some existing ones, and rebalanced others to create a smoother experience and better progression through the Reward Pass.
Outpost
Fixed an issue where the Workshop screen could appear broken if the basic workbench was placed in the last available Outpost slot.
Your Raider is now hidden when inspecting or decorating furniture and when viewing a bench’s Generator screen, preventing the camera from being blocked.
The camera rotation, in the Inspect/Decorate view, now requires holding the left mouse button; right mouse drags no longer adjust the camera pitch.
Fixed an issue where the Inspect/Decorate camera could fade to black when orbiting near walls.
Skill Tree
Node tooltips now show how many levels there are for a skill. Visible as long as the node has not been reached.
Changed wording from 'Add Skill Point' to 'Spend Point' to minimize confusion.
Weapon Amplification
Updated the Weapon Bench upgrade tab: the button for amplified weapons now reads "Amplify" instead of "Ascend".
Fixed a visual issue where the Aphelion’s beam effect could appear cut off.
Improved explosion impact marks with higher-resolution visuals for clearer craters.
Fixed an issue where the smoke from firing a weapon could disappear under certain circumstances.
The Raider Tool has the default skin even when other skins are equipped.
Extracting with partial progress of ‘To The Skies’ quest may result in an inability to complete it.
‘When Everything Falls’ - some quest objectives, such as “Photograph Port A” may not complete for some players.
In some instances, if players lose or sell quest items, such as the Equatorial Sundial needed for ‘Clean Hands’, the quest cannot be completed.
Players can still die after entering the Ballistic Gondola if they are downed and very close to being knocked out.
Some XBOX players may experience instability or crashes.
The Grapple Hook can, in rare instances, cause the player using it to be thrown upwards at high speed.
The Grapple Hook cannot be thrown while inside of the Matriarch’s shield.
ARC Reclaimers can occasionally fail to dock on the appropriate spot on the Frigate.
See you Topside,
The ARC Raiders Team
Raiders!
We’re rolling out a hotfix right now to address several instances that allowed players to access locked rooms and duplicate items.

A big thank you to everyone who reported these issues directly to us! Reports through our Discord support inbox or @ScrappyMail allow us to act on these issues much more effectively without spreading the method publicly. You’re helping keep the game fair and fun for everyone.

Update 2.1 is going live right now and marks the start of the PvE toggle Beta Test! We know that the announcement of this highly requested feature has sparked both excitement and skepticism so jump in, try it out, and let us know what you think. Your feedback, along with the in-game data, will help us decide if the toggle becomes a permanent part of the game.
https://arcraiders.com/news/pve-toggle-what-to-know
The Carrion Set is available at the store together with a number of content and bug fixes:
Fixed an issue where character models would sometimes appear enlarged.
Fixed an issue where vaulting onto destroyed ARC parts could launch you or debris into the air; vaults on Matriarch, Vaporizer, Hydra, and Firefly remains are now stable.
Character animations will now have a short cooldown before they swap sides on repeated shoulder swapping.
Reduced overly loud footstep sounds when outdoors and balanced footstep volume across different surfaces.
Added clearer visual and audio feedback when melee hits land on weak points, making successful strikes easier to recognize.
Fixed an issue where shoulder swapping repeatedly could make footsteps audio not play.
Added sound effects to the Cowboy emote.
Made several more subtle audio improvements and additions.
Frigate hatches now inflict burning damage over time when they open.
Smoothed collision on Frigate cargo to prevent getting stuck on curved surfaces.
The Frigate cargo drop has been adjusted to prevent unintended knockouts.
Fixed unintended interactions between throwables and certain doors on the Emperor.
The missing Zenith Outfit toggles will be granted to all players that have completed their fifth Expedition.
Equipped weapon stencils now display their rarity in the weapon tooltip.
Fixed an issue where the Broad Shoulders skill did not activate on spawn, preventing sprinting despite being within the increased carry limit; inventory weight now updates correctly after loading in.
Fixed an issue where the Field Repair skill could fail to work after unlocking it if you had already played a round in the same session. Restarting is no longer required for it to take effect.
Fixed an issue where the camera would shake violently when another player or vegetation came between the player and the camera while firing.
Fixed an issue where weight values would initially be calculated incorrectly after loading into a round.
Fixed an issue where Fight or Flight would incorrectly bypass the penalty from Sprinting on Fumes.
General
Mobile-Fire Grip Fittings now correctly require Skulker Targeters to research, instead of Skulker Drivers.
Stamina-restoring consumables can no longer be used while the Sprinting on Fumes cooldown is active.

One of the important balancing considerations for Sprinting on Fumes was the penalty that is applied once the ability has ceased. Having items that could bypass that penalty entirely disrupts the intended risk of using the skill.
Grappling Hook

Made it easier to vault onto ledges and roofs when using the Grappling Hook, especially on Pendola Pass. Auto-vault now triggers more reliably at the top of rope climbs, and ending a swing on walkable ground is more consistent.
Fixed several issues that occurred when the Grappling Hook let players swing from objects too light to hold their weight.
Fixed an issue where the Grappling Hook could detach when tethered to fast‑moving objects like the Ballistic Gondola, causing the line to break during lift‑off.
The Grappling Hook rope now wraps around geometry while the hook is in flight.
Fixed an issue where Grappling Hooks and Tether Launchers would not release when the player was downed by fall damage.
Fixed an issue where Grappling Hooks and Tether Launchers with 0 durability would be destroyed instead of broken.
General
Adjusted spawns during Frigate rounds to avoid starting too far from the action under certain circumstances.
Improved vaulting and traversal on rocky terrain to reduce unintended sliding after climbing.
Fixed world props in a tunnel sometimes disappearing when viewed from above.
Improved lighting and reflections in Frigate areas and on Dam Battlegrounds to reduce visual artifacts and improve performance.
Improved shelter door interactions to prevent players from being squeezed when opening them, with more space provided next to the door.
Fixed several collision and clipping issues, gaps, and stuck spots across several maps.
Pendola Pass
Fixed an issue where players could be eliminated despite being inside the Gondola and extracting.
Polished terrain and collision on Pendola Pass—fixed gaps, clipping, and hard-to-traverse spots, reduced visual pop-in, and blocked unintended areas.
Fixed a traversal spot in the Railyard on Pendola Pass where you couldn’t jump up or auto step up as expected.
Polished Pendola Pass with collision and visual fixes, corrected footstep and impact sounds on station canopies, and improved VFX culling to prevent effects showing through surfaces.
Adjusted interior snow and terrain blending to prevent landscape from clipping into buildings.
Adjusted night lighting to be darker with reduced visibility.
Adjusted ARC Frigate cargo drop points in Pendola Pass to improve accessibility and prevent clipping.
Reduced memory usage to improve stability on Spaceport, Buried City, and Dam Battlegrounds, with particular benefits on Xbox Series S.
General
Extended compass and map visibility distance for Gondola markers from 120 to 175 meters.
Improved placement of pings on the Skulker and Bully when marked from long range.
In the Weapon Amplification tree, hovering or focusing an upgrade now highlights the path to that node, unless it’s blocked.
Fixed a bug where spectating could fail to show your squadmates’ HUD info, making it appear they had no Shield.
Added a new indicator and seen-state tracking for weapon stencils in the customization screen, making newly acquired stencils easier to spot and manage.
Reward Pass
Fixed an issue where the Reward Pass would not progress correctly. The End-Of-Round Reward Pass screen no longer mistakenly counts milestones from previous rounds.
Polished the Reward Pass completion screen: updated button labels, fixed an incorrect premium icon on non-upgrade buttons, and adjusted layout to prevent image cropping and text overflow.
Fixed the Reward Pass tile overstating completed levels and aligned the completion icon and “Completed” label.
The Reward Pass details screen now shows the name of the active pass.
Outpost
Fixed an issue where Outpost module recipes would remain in the tracker after installing.
Added an orange indicator to the Outpost tab when a project step is completed, making new updates easier to spot.
Fixed an issue where leaving Customization in the Outpost could leave the view out of focus.
Fixed an issue where exiting decorating in a module room returned you to the base room instead of the room you were editing.
Skill Tree
Fixed an issue where the Field Salvaging skill could fail to display the right items if unlocked after playing a round in the same session.
Fixed an issue where camera movement could be prevented if Field Salvaging or Field Repair were interrupted.
Fixed a bug where End of Round inventory weight and max loadout weight did not reflect character skills like Reduced Weapon Encumbrance or Max Carry Weight.
Fixed quest objective progress bars displaying incorrectly whilst in Speranza.
Fixed an issue where visiting loot‑icon areas in Pendola Pass did not count toward the “Picking Up the Pieces” quest objective.
Cinematics for “Sizing Things Up” correctly play after quest completion.
Fixed issue where the Semi-Auto Amplification for the Hairpin did not deal reduced headshot damage.
See you Topside,
The ARC Raiders Team
Raiders!
We are now deploying a hotfix to address a few issues that popped up after yesterday's update. Please restart your game to download!
Fixed an issue where weapon meshes became partially invisible when equipped with weapon attachments.
Fixed an issue where weapon models were not showing in the inventory.
Fixed several instances causing server crashes.
Fixed an issue that could cause players to fall through a grate on Pendola Pass and get stuck.

notes.title: Frozen Trail is coming - tune in for a First Look!

items.text: In case you missed it, we’ll be holding a First Look at Frozen Trail and what’s coming with the update tomorrow! On September 23rd, at 10am PDT (7pm CEST), tune in for an extended peek at our biggest update yet.
Can’t wait to hear what you think! We’ve got more planned ahead of October 8th, stay tuned.
Fixed an issue where the Rawhide outfit’s headgear would remain on when toggled off in Customization.
Door blockers will no longer create a copy of their mesh on the opposite side from the direction they are applied.
Fixed an issue where keyboard input could stop working after launching unfocused or returning from background, ensuring keyboard controls reliably respond when refocusing the window.
Fixed an issue where doors could become out of sync in some cases, making them appear open to the player whilst actually being closed.

Fixed an issue where swapping or splitting items could place them into incompatible containers (such as forcing non-quick-use items into the belt), and added safeguards against invalid inventory slot indexing in the inventory.
Buried City
Fixed an issue where lighting in Buried City could appear overly dark or missing, improving overall visibility.

items.text: While our dev team is hard at work putting the finishing touches on Frozen Trail, our Anti-Cheat team is making constant updates and improvements across the board to our Fair Play initiatives.

We also continue sanctioning abnormally high-value item transfers. Item duplication is also on our minds, and we’re seeing positive outcomes following this summer’s ongoing improvements on that front.

We are constantly working on ways to prevent serial cheaters and discourage them from returning. Currently, we're strengthening our policies when it comes to shared licenses and how those are restricted when an account is sanctioned. In practice, this will make it harder for cheaters who were detected on one account to purchase another. Keeping track of a cheater's behavior before and after receiving a sanction helps us anticipate it and act faster in the future.

Previously, we mentioned the speed of action against unfair play is important to us. To that end, we have been improving our detection systems and we are extending first-strike permanent bans. This allows us to catch offenders much quicker with a very high degree of confidence.

notes.title: A Note on Third Party Software

items.text: When we see reports of third party software being used to gain an advantage of any kind, in-game or at account level, we investigate. The first and most important step is to verify the validity of the report and whether or not the software actually does what it claims to do. A lot of the time, claims are just that, and interacting with this kind of software carries a large amount of risk.

Be aware that downloading unverified and unofficial software can put more than just your account at risk. Beyond getting banned and losing access to the game, your data and personal information could be exposed.

Remember that your account is only as secure as its weakest link. In order to protect your account, your purchases and progression, we strongly recommend making sure 2FA or passkeys are enabled on all external accounts connected to your Embark ID. Oh, and never share your credentials with anyone. No matter how many ducks they offer.

Over the past few weeks, we have been making several improvements alongside Anybrain and Denuvo Anti-Cheat. This has resulted in swift action being taken against a large number of accounts that were using recently popularized cheating software.

There is also the matter of ensuring permanent sanctions for serial, blatant cheaters. We continue working on methods that make it more difficult for new accounts to be obtained and that discourage cheaters from returning.

There have been compounding improvements in our ability to also detect accounts that participated in what we classify as “economy exploits”, which means we can more quickly sanction offenders. These types of sanctions have been ongoing.

Additionally, we have several simultaneous initiatives that are meant to address teaming and general matchmaking abuse. We know how important having a consistently good experience is, and that in certain regions or at certain times, it’s easier to run into groups of players that try to force their way into lobbies and engage in griefing. We’ll share more when all of these are ready.

And that’s, of course, not all. We’ll keep building up all of the initiatives we mentioned and we’ll do our best to make sure that your experiences across the Rust Belt are fun, thrilling, and most importantly fair.

Greetings Raiders!

Live Update 1.39.0 is going out right now, bringing various game fixes, changes & additional updates to the Matchmaking System. The Seeker & Wolfpack should no longer deal inconsistent damage and trinkets previously added in 1.33.0 can now stack! Additionally, you can find the new Dweller Outfit in the store.
Over the past months, improving matchmaking has been one of our top priorities. We’ve introduced various adjustments and improvements based on your feedback & requests.

Since our Notes on The Matchmaking System, one change has stood out with the community: defending yourself is no longer treated the same as starting a fight. It meant self-defense still counted toward your playstyle estimate, but with much less weight than starting a fight. Your feedback was positive, and many of you have asked us to take it further.

The most common follow-up request we've seen is to remove the impact of Defensive PvP entirely - going from reduced weight to none at all. Starting now, we're testing exactly that. During the test, only the fights you choose to start will influence your playstyle estimate, and defending yourself won't affect it at all. This includes knocking out enemies who attacked you first.
So what counts as starting a fight, and what counts as defending yourself? Here's how the system reads an encounter:
Who's defending: If the other squad damages, downs, or knocks out any of your squadmates first, your whole squad counts as defending - the squad that strikes first is the one that started the fight.

How it's weighed: The more serious the encounter, the more it counts. A drawn-out firefight - with more damage dealt and raiders downed - weighs heavily, while a stray accidental hit or a brief exchange where the other squad flees after minimal damage still counts as starting a fight but weighs far less.
Third-partying: Jumping into a fight between other squads that's already underway counts as starting a fight, too.
Over the coming weeks we'll monitor our matchmaking metrics, watch how PvP develops Topside, and gather your feedback.

Two earlier changes are also still live: the Solo, Duo, and Trio matchmaking tracking from 1.36.0 and the matchmaking optimization adjustments from 1.38.0. We're keeping a close watch on how both perform, but telemetry only tells us half the story - to get the full picture, we need to hear how your matches actually feel.
The latest matchmaking survey covers all of this, so take a minute to fill it out - your input is the other half, and it's what turns our data into better decisions. Thank you, Raiders!

items.text: Attention Raiders!
We have an important update about the future of ARC Raiders.
We’ve seen your questions and your speculation about what’s coming next. We’re working on something major, and we’re able to share a few details about it today.

Frozen Trail will be our biggest, most exciting update yet. The goal is to provide new ways to progress and reasons to play, while bringing meaningful additions to the game’s loop, gameplay and world. This includes, but is by no means limited to:
The largest map yet,
Our most ambitious ARC Operation so far - expect unique behaviors and designs!
New Systems of Progression,
Improved Skill Tree,
Alongside new weapons, items, instruments, cosmetics and more!

It’s an ambitious update which will take time to do right. To achieve this vision and focus our efforts, we’re going to deliver content updates twice a year moving forward. However, you can still expect regular live updates for bug fixing, balancing, store updates and more.
Read all about why we’re doing this and what it means for ARC Raiders, and get a peek at our next major update, Frozen Trail: https://arcraiders.com/news/development-update

Balance Changes
Weapon Economy Adjustments

The weapon economy has increasingly started looking more and more unbalanced, where players engaging in heavy PVP have to make a lot of difficult decisions around their weapons while the most friendly players have ended up in a chronic state of weapon accumulation. We want to balance this out so that all players are challenged by weapon attrition, as well as introducing new ways to combat it.
New feature: Repair on upgrade

Weapon upgrading becomes very expensive when you feel like you have to repair the weapon beforehand, making it less accessible than we would like. To give more ways to repair low durability weapons and elevate the upgrade loop:
Upgrading weapons will now repair 25% of the weapons max durability
Weapon drop & durability
We're reducing weapon spawn around the outskirts of the maps to increase value and tension of high tier areas and locked rooms.
We're also increasing the range of durability a weapon can spawn with, as well as reducing the average outside of locked rooms. This should be easily recouped by the new repair on upgrade.
Avg durability on spawned weapons: 50 -> 30
These changes mean that you might find a weapon on the outskirts with 15 durability but will still find weapons around 60 durability in locked rooms.
Weapon durability loss on shot

We've heard a clear frustration that maintaining high tier weapons is very expensive compared to the lower tier ones. We want high tier weapons to have more longevity compared to low tier weapons, so we're adjusting durability loss on shot to match this:
Common weapons: +75% durability loss on shot
Uncommon weapons: +50% durability loss on shot
Rare weapons: +35% durability loss on shot
Epic weapons: -5% durability loss on shot
Legendary weapons: -10% durability loss on shot
Weapon durability loss on being knocked out
We want heavy PVP to be a viable way to play ARC Raiders, and to align this playstyle with other ways to play, we're reducing durability loss on weapons when a player is knocked out by 50%.

In 1.13 we shipped an update that included an optimization fix for our weapons, but as many of you noticed this had the unforeseen consequence of lowering the total fire-rate of semi-automatic weapons. In 1.13.1 we reverted that fix, but something else made it into the update that shouldn't have.

Many of you have reported a "shadow buff" to the weapons, and after investigating it we found that 1.13.1 had inadvertently impacted our weapon input buffers. Where you previously would have to time your inputs to the intended cadence of a weapon to reach its full potential, you could now instead spam-click the button, effectively bypassing any skill requirement to learn the weapon's cadence. We want to keep some of that skill expression, but we also recognize that what we had previously didn't feel very responsive. To address that and land in some sort of middle ground, we have since added more levers for us to control the weapon input buffering window on a gun-to-gun basis, and we've adjusted the semi-automatic weapons accordingly. The weapons should now still be more responsive to fire when spam-clicking, but the players who choose to pace their shots will see better results.

In addition to these changes, we've also been looking into the balance between our low tier and high tier weapons. A lot of you have expressed concerns that some low tier weapons outperform our higher tier weapons at significantly reduced cost, and we're hoping to shift that balance a bit while still keeping some of that flexibility to punch above your weight if you are skilled enough. We're starting by reducing the overall TTK of the Stitcher and Kettle, and increasing the maneuverability of the Aphelion and Jupiter. We're also taking a second stab at the Venator, which still seems to be dominating a lot of our PvP encounters.
Stitcher

Dev Note: The Stitcher has played its role well as a close quarter weapon that rewards thoughtful positioning, but we've found that its fast TTK can sometimes lead to situations where you're ambushed and killed before you have much time to react. As many of you have pointed out, the high headshot damage is a large contributor to this problem. The TTK is often fine when the weapon is aimed at the center of mass, but when you get close enough to land the majority of the shots in your target's head, we see TTK numbers that are much faster than other weapons. These changes aim to bring that headshot TTK a bit closer to the body shot TTK by both reducing the full-spray accuracy of the weapon, and reducing the headshot multiplier.

Increased Per Shot Dispersion by around 50% (Making it bloom faster)
Kettle

Dev Note: The Kettle has been in a bit of a weird place. Its high damage output was intended to be used in a more medium range setting at a more deliberate pace, but we see many of you bringing it up in close quarters and effectively turning into an SMG. We want to distinguish it more from the Stitcher, but we also see that you enjoy the versatility of this weapon. So we're reducing the base damage to bring its TTK more in line, but we're keeping the high headshot multiplier to see if we can push players to go for more headshots.
Reduced Base Damage from 10 to 8.5
Venator

Dev Note: Since the last nerfs to the Venator in 1.3.0, we've kept an eye on our data to see how it performs. During this time many of you have raised concerns that it's still dominating in PVP, and our data has shown that it is one of the highest performing weapons in the game right now. For a weapon of this tier we want it to perform well, but maybe not this well. We're looking at an overall nerf to its damage to bring down its TTK, and if that doesn't work we might need to look into its ammo consumption and cost efficiency.

Jupiter

Dev Note: In PVP, the Jupiter does the most headshot damage in the game, but it's quite difficult to hit headshots with it at longer ranges. You're also quite vulnerable when you use it in closer ranges since missing one shot will make you a sitting target until you either reload or swap weapons. We're increasing how much you zoom when you use ADS to give you a better view of the targets you're trying to hit, and we're reducing its equip and unequip time to make it easier to swap to a secondary weapon to follow up on your shot.

It was intended to be a more PVP focused legendary weapon, but it couldn't quite keep up with the pacing of many of our other PVP weapons. We've made some changes to make it feel less bulky and a bit more nimble to use, to make it more viable in PVP.

When we shared our last update about tackling unfair play, we didn’t fully convey the complexity and scale of what goes into cheat detection. Our defenses operate on multiple levels: some checks are simple and definitive, while others are behavioral and data-driven and evolve over time. We also leverage broad gameplay telemetry and machine learning techniques to spot patterns that aren’t obvious at first glance. These methods take longer to develop, must adapt as game systems change, and don’t always offer instant certainty the way blunt software detections can.

We’ve recently taken action against different exploits and we are further tightening our rules and stepping up enforcement. Serious infractions now carry stricter consequences. Strong detections will receive permanent bans right off the bat, while others will receive a temporary suspension and a single chance to correct the behavior. Recent updates to Family Sharing have strengthened our ability to curb misconduct and streamlined the removal of bad actors from the game. We are preparing to launch a systematic manual review of ban appeals. The game is young and the volume of telemetry is enormous, but this process ensures every case is handled with care as we continue to learn quickly and invest heavily in the precision of our enforcement tools.
Our dedicated anti-cheat team works tirelessly to keep the game fair. It’s an ongoing fight, and we’re committed to it.
//Ossen

Venator

Dev note: The fully upgraded Venator has been over-performing recently, capable of outgunning full squads using close range weapons. We’re re-tuning the fire-rate gained from upgrades to pull down the pacing a bit, while still keeping its damage and accuracy intact. This should encourage players to take some more time with their shots rather than mag-dumping the first poor soul they encounter. The community also rightfully pointed out that the weight of the Venator was inconsistent with the weights of our other pistols, so we’ve corrected that as well.

Explosive Damage

Dev note: We noticed that explosives dealt damage to more parts at once than intended, allowing weapons like the Hullcracker to kill larger drones too quickly. We’ve adjusted explosive damage to make it more consistent across the board, and we’ve re-balanced the damage of the Hullcracker to account for that change. This will require Hullcracker shots to need a bit more precision while still dealing good damage to the targeted spot.
